body:
## Problem
A floating preview window (hover, signature help) converted to a normal
window (e.g. with CTRL-W_H or nvim_win_set_config()) is still closed by
the open_floating_preview() autocommands, and a later preview may focus
or close it as if it were still a float.

Closes #36659

## Solution
When the preview window is no longer floating, remove its auto-close
autocommands and stop tracking it as the buffer's floating preview.

comment_data.body: The converted window still has the `focus_id` window variable set (nothing removes it), so without this check, calling `open_floating_preview()` while focused in the converted window runs `wincmd p` and jumps away instead of opening a new float. I added a test covering this.
comment_data.diff_hunk:

     if opts.focus_id and opts.focusable ~= false and opts.focus then
       -- Go back to previous window if we are in a focusable one
       local current_winnr = api.nvim_get_current_win()
-      if vim.w[current_winnr][opts.focus_id] then
+      if vim.w[current_winnr][opts.focus_id] and is_float(current_winnr) then

comment_data.body: The narrowing is intentional: a window converted to a normal split should not be refocused, so we leave it alone and open a fresh float instead (covered by the tests). It was still safe for invalid windows since `win_gettype()` returns `"unknown"` for them, but I have made the validity check explicit in `is_float()` to make that clear.
